records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֡ר בָּֽעֲרָבָה֩ מ֨וֹל ס֜וּף בֵּֽין־פָּארָ֧ן וּבֵֽין־תֹּ֛פֶל וְלָבָ֥ן וַחֲצֵרֹ֖ת וְדִ֥י זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: These [are] the words which spoke Moses to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah, opposite Suph, between Paran and between Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Di-zahab.
pieces: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness across the Jordan: in the Arabah facing Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

L.1: These [are] the words that Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

R.1: These are the words that Moses spoke to all the people of Israel across the Jordan River. They were in the wilderness, in the Arabah, the low valley, near Suph. The place was between Paran and the places called Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

decisions.choice: These are the words: the opening of Moses' farewell speeches, given in Moab, across the Jordan, in the fortieth year
decisions.reason: The book begins by naming what it holds: words that Moses spoke to the whole people. Verses 3-5 then fix the time and place. It is the fortieth year after the departure from Egypt (verse 3), after the victories over Sihon and Og (verse 4), and Israel is camped in the land of Moab, east of the Jordan (verse 5), on the edge of the land that Moses himself will not enter (verse 37; 34:1-5). Most of the book is Moses speaking; the narrator's own voice is heard only in a few places (1:1-5; 4:41-49; 5:1; and parts of chapters 27-34). The Hebrew name of the book, "Words", comes from this opening line.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: the region east of the river, named from the viewpoint of the land to the west
decisions.reason: The phrase means "on the other side of the Jordan". Here it is the land east of the river, where Israel was camped in the plains of Moab (verse 5; Numbers 22:1). It is named as seen from the land west of the Jordan, the land of Canaan that God had promised to Israel, so that the east side is "across" the river. The same phrase can point the other way: when Moses, standing in the east, speaks of the land Israel will enter, "across the Jordan" means the west (3:20, 25; 11:30). The phrase names a region; by itself it does not say where the speaker or the writer was standing.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, Suph, Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, Di-zahab: the rift valley and places whose sites are mostly unknown
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley that runs from the Sea of Galilee south through the Jordan and the Dead Sea to the gulf at Elath; here it is the part of it in Moab, opposite Jericho (Numbers 22:1). Paran is the wilderness south of Canaan (Numbers 10:12; 13:26), and Hazeroth was a camp on the way from Sinai (Numbers 11:35; 33:17). Suph, Tophel, Laban and Di-zahab cannot be located today; Suph may be connected with the name of the Sea of Reeds. The list may describe the region where Moses spoke, or it may recall places on the journey from Horeb; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, the low valley
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name and adds a short description, because "Arabah" means nothing to most readers. It also adds "River" to "the Jordan" and breaks the long list of places into short sentences.

records.heading: The words Moses spoke across the Jordan

records.source: אַחַ֨ד עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ מֵֽחֹרֵ֔ב דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַר־שֵׂעִ֑יר עַ֖ד קָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: Eleven day[s] from Horeb, [by the] way of mount Seir, to Kadesh-barnea.
pieces: It is eleven days' journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the Mount Seir road.

L.2: Eleven days [it is] from Horeb, by the way of Mount Seir, to Kadesh-barnea.

R.2: The trip from Horeb, the mountain also called Sinai, to Kadesh-barnea takes eleven days along the road through the hills of Seir.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain of God, also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Horeb is the mountain where God appeared to Moses in the bush (Exodus 3:1) and where he made his covenant with Israel (4:10, 15; 5:2). Exodus and Numbers usually call it Sinai (Exodus 19:11; Numbers 10:12); Deuteronomy calls it Horeb.

decisions.choice: the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea: the route north through the region of Edom to the oasis on the southern edge of Canaan
decisions.reason: Mount Seir is the hill country of Edom, south of the Dead Sea (2:1, 4-5; Genesis 36:8). Kadesh-barnea, often simply Kadesh, was an oasis at the edge of the wilderness of Paran and Zin, south of the land of Canaan. The spies were sent from there and Israel later camped there (Numbers 13:26; 20:1; 32:8).

decisions.choice: eleven days: a short journey set against the forty years of verse 3
decisions.reason: Placed beside the date in verse 3, the distance makes a point: the way from Horeb to the edge of the land took eleven days, but Israel reached the land only in the fortieth year. Verses 19-46 tell why: at Kadesh the people refused to go in, and that generation wandered until it died out (Numbers 14:33-34).

decisions.choice: Horeb, the mountain also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Readable adds the better known name so that readers recognize the mountain of the Ten Commandments.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ בְּאַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֖דֶשׁ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹת֖וֹ אֲלֵהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] fortieth year, in [the] eleventh month, on [the] first of the month, spoke Moses to [the] sons of Israel according to all that had commanded Yahweh him for them.
pieces: On the first day of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year, Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and told them everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to give them.

L.3: And it was in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first [day] of the month, [that] Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him for them.

R.3: Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} on the first day of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year after they left Egypt. He told them everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to tell them.

decisions.choice: the fortieth year, the eleventh month, the first day: forty years after the departure from Egypt, near the end of that year
decisions.reason: The years are counted from the departure from Egypt, as in Numbers 33:38, where Aaron dies in the fortieth year. The date leaves about two months before the crossing of the Jordan in the first month of the next year (Joshua 4:19), time enough for Moses' speeches, his death, and thirty days of mourning (34:8).

decisions.choice: according to all that the LORD had commanded him: Moses passes on God's own commands
decisions.reason: What Moses is about to say is not his own program. He speaks as the one who received God's words at Horeb and hands them on to the people (5:5, 27-31; 18:18).

decisions.choice: after they left Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says from what point the forty years are counted, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader (see the meaning decision).

records.source: אַחֲרֵ֣י הַכֹּת֗וֹ אֵ֚ת סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וְאֵ֗ת ע֚וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁר־יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּעַשְׁתָּרֹ֖ת בְּאֶדְרֶֽעִי׃
records.gloss: After his striking Sihon, king of the Amorite[s], who [was] dwelling in Heshbon, and Og, king of the Bashan, who [was] dwelling in Ashtaroth, in Edrei.
pieces: This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, whose city was Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, whose cities were Ashtaroth and Edrei.

L.4: [It was] after he had struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtaroth, in Edrei.

R.4: This was after Moses had defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from the city of Heshbon. He had also defeated Og, king of Bashan, who ruled from the cities of Ashtaroth and Edrei.

decisions.choice: he struck: Moses, as Israel's leader
decisions.reason: The subject is Moses, the last person named (verse 3). The victories belong to Israel under his leadership, and Moses himself will say that it was the LORD who gave these kings into their hands (2:24, 31-36; 3:1-3).

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og: the two kings east of the Jordan whose lands Israel had just taken
decisions.reason: Sihon ruled the land of the Amorites between the Arnon and the Jabbok rivers from his city Heshbon; Og ruled Bashan, the high plain farther north, east of the Sea of Galilee (Numbers 21:21-35). Their defeat gave Israel its first land, later given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (3:12-17), and it is often recalled as a sign of what God will do west of the Jordan (2:24-3:11; 31:4).

decisions.choice: in Ashtaroth, in Edrei: Og's two royal cities
alternatives: who lived in Ashtaroth, when he defeated him at Edrei
decisions.reason: Joshua 12:4 and 13:12 say that Og reigned "in Ashtaroth and in Edrei", so the two names here are read as his two cities. The words could also mean that Moses defeated Og at Edrei, where the battle was fought (3:1; Numbers 21:33).

decisions.choice: who ruled from
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the kings "sat" or "dwelt" in these cities. For a king that means the city where he had his throne, so Readable says "ruled from".

records.source: בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֑ב הוֹאִ֣יל מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֵּאֵ֛ר אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: Across the Jordan, in [the] land of Moab, undertook Moses [to] make clear the law the this, saying,
pieces: Across the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses set about explaining this law. He said,

L.5: Across the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to set out this law clearly, saying,

R.5: There, across the Jordan River in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this teaching. He said,

decisions.choice: torah, this law: instruction, the whole of what Moses teaches in this book, not only its rules
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to point the way or to teach, and it names instruction, as a parent's teaching is called by this word (Proverbs 1:8; 3:1). "This law" in Deuteronomy is the whole body of Moses' teaching: the story of what God has done for Israel, the call to love him and keep his covenant, and the statutes and rulings that go with it (4:44-45; 17:18-19; 31:9-12). It contains commands, but it is more than a code of laws.

decisions.choice: make clear: explain, set out plainly
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something plain and easy to read. It is used of writing the law "very plainly" on stones (27:8) and of writing a vision plainly on tablets (Habakkuk 2:2). Moses is not giving another law but setting out and explaining God's instruction for the people who are about to enter the land.

decisions.choice: undertook: set himself to the task, began
decisions.reason: The verb means to make up one's mind to do something, to venture on it, as Abraham does when he dares to speak to God (Genesis 18:27). Moses now begins the long task of teaching.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan, in the land of Moab: the plains of Moab opposite Jericho
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "across the Jordan" is the east side of the river. The place is the plains of Moab across from Jericho, where Israel was camped at the end of Numbers (Numbers 22:1; 36:13), in land that had once been Moab's.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "law". Readable says "teaching", because "law" by itself makes most readers think only of rules, and what follows begins with history and appeal (see the meaning decision).

records.source: יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֵ֖ינוּ בְּחֹרֵ֣ב לֵאמֹ֑ר רַב־לָכֶ֥ם שֶׁ֖בֶת בָּהָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Yahweh our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, Enough for you [the] staying at the mountain the this.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God spoke to us at Horeb and said, 'Your time at this mountain has been long enough.

L.6: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, '[It is] enough for you [to have] stayed at this mountain.

R.6: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God spoke to us at Mount Horeb. He said, 'You have been camped by this mountain long enough.

decisions.choice: the LORD our God spoke to us: Moses' first speech begins here and runs to 4:40
decisions.reason: The narrator's introduction (verses 1-5) ends, and Moses speaks. His first speech looks back over the journey from Horeb to Moab (1:6-3:29) and then calls the people to obey (4:1-40). Within it he quotes God, the people and his own earlier words.

decisions.choice: our God ... to us: the generation in Moab spoken of as the people who were at Horeb
decisions.reason: Most of those Moses addresses were children at Horeb or not yet born (verses 35, 39). He still says that God spoke "to us", because Israel is addressed as one people through its generations, and the covenant made at Horeb is theirs too (5:2-3).

decisions.choice: you have stayed at this mountain: the year or so Israel spent at Horeb
decisions.reason: Israel reached the mountain in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1) and left in the second month of the second year (Numbers 10:11-12). There God gave the covenant and the laws and the tabernacle was built. Now it is time to move toward the land.

decisions.choice: long enough
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "much for you", that is, it has been enough. Balanced and Readable say "long enough", because the point is the length of the stay.

records.source: פְּנ֣וּ׀וּסְע֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם וּבֹ֨אוּ הַ֥ר הָֽאֱמֹרִי֮ וְאֶל־כָּל־שְׁכֵנָיו֒ בָּעֲרָבָ֥ה בָהָ֛ר וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֥ה וּבַנֶּ֖גֶב וּבְח֣וֹף הַיָּ֑ם אֶ֤רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַלְּבָנ֔וֹן עַד־הַנָּהָ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל נְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃
records.gloss: Turn and set out for yourselves and go [to the] hill country of the Amorite[s] and to all its neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, and in the Shephelah, and in the Negev, and on [the] coast of the sea, [the] land of the Canaanite[s], and the Lebanon, as far as the river the great, [the] river Euphrates.
pieces: Turn and move on. Go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all the regions near it: the Arabah, the hill country, the foothills, the Negev and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.

L.7: Turn and set out for yourselves, and go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all its neighbors, in the Arabah, in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Negev and on the shore of the sea, the land of the Canaanites, and the Lebanon, up to the great river, the river Euphrates.

R.7: Break camp and go on your way. Go into the hill country where the Amorites live and to all the places around it: the Jordan Valley, the hills, the low hills in the west, the southern desert and the seacoast. Go into the land of the Canaanites and into Lebanon, as far as the great Euphrates River.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, the hill country, the Shephelah, the Negev, the coast: the regions of the land, from east to west and south
decisions.reason: The list names the parts of the land as Israel knew them: the Arabah, the Jordan valley in the east; the central hill country; the Shephelah, the low hills between the hills and the coastal plain; the Negev, the dry south; and the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. Lebanon is the mountain range to the north.

decisions.choice: as far as the great river, the Euphrates: the full extent of the land promised to Abraham
decisions.reason: These are the borders God promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18), repeated in Exodus 23:31, Deuteronomy 11:24 and Joshua 1:4. They mark the whole of the promise, wider than the land Israel would hold in Joshua's day.

decisions.choice: Amorites, Canaanites: names for the peoples living in the land
decisions.reason: "Amorites" here means the peoples of the hill country of Canaan in general (verses 19-20, 27, 44; Genesis 15:16), and "Canaanites" those of the lowlands and coast (Numbers 13:29). Both names can stand for all the inhabitants of the land.

decisions.choice: Break camp and go on your way
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "turn and set out". Readable uses the plain words for leaving a camp. Readable also describes the regions instead of naming them ("the low hills in the west" for the Shephelah, "the southern desert" for the Negev).

records.source: רְאֵ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ בֹּ֚אוּ וּרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֣ע יְ֠הוָה לַאֲבֹ֨תֵיכֶ֜ם לְאַבְרָהָ֨ם לְיִצְחָ֤ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב֙ לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֔ם וּלְזַרְעָ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: See, I have set before you the land; go in and take possession of the land which swore Yahweh to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their offspring after them.
pieces: Look, I have placed the land in front of you. Go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.'

L.8: See, I have set before you the land. Go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, that [he would] give [it] to them and to their offspring after them.'

R.8: Look, the land is in front of you, and I am giving it to you. Go in and take it as your own. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, made a promise with an oath to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I promised to give this land to them and to their descendants after them.'

decisions.choice: take possession of: take over the land and hold it as your own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over property and hold it, as an heir does. It runs through Deuteronomy: Israel is to go in and take possession of the land God gives (verse 21; 4:1; 6:18). Used of nations, the same verb means to drive them out.

decisions.choice: the oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: God's sworn promise of the land
decisions.reason: God promised the land to Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 15:18-21) and confirmed it with an oath (Genesis 22:16-17; 26:3; 50:24). Deuteronomy often recalls this oath as the ground of Israel's hope (6:10, 18; 7:8).

decisions.choice: the LORD swore: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: The words are still God's, begun in verse 6, but God names himself in the third person, "the land that the LORD swore". This is a common way for God to speak of his own promises in the Old Testament; it does not mean that another speaker has taken over.

decisions.choice: See ... I have set: the land is as good as given
decisions.reason: "See" is addressed to the people as one (the Hebrew uses the singular), and the following verbs are plural. "I have set" is the language of a done deal: the land lies open, already given, and Israel has only to go in.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that God is still speaking about himself, where Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's "the LORD swore".

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fathers", here meaning forefathers. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", the ordinary word for those who came before.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל לְבַדִּ֖י שְׂאֵ֥ת אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I said to you at the time the that, saying, Not I am able by myself to bear you.
pieces: Back then I told you, 'Carrying all of you on my own is more than I can do.

L.9: And I said to you at that time, 'I am not able by myself to bear you.

R.9: At that time I said to you, 'I cannot take care of all of you by myself.

decisions.choice: at that time I said: the appointment of leaders, told also in Exodus 18 and Numbers 11
decisions.reason: Exodus 18:13-26 tells how Moses, on the advice of his father-in-law Jethro, chose capable men to judge the people with him, and Numbers 11:14-17 how Moses said he could not carry the people alone and the LORD gave seventy elders to share the load. Moses here recalls these events in his own way, as his own proposal to the people, without naming Jethro. "At that time" is the time at Horeb, before the people set out.

decisions.choice: to bear you: to carry the load of leading the people
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift and carry. Here the load is the work of leading the people and settling their quarrels (verse 12), the same picture Moses uses in Numbers 11:11-14.

records.source: יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם הִרְבָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְהִנְּכֶ֣ם הַיּ֔וֹם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: Yahweh your God has multiplied you, and here you [are] today like [the] stars of the heavens for multitude.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has increased your numbers, and look at you today: as many as the stars in the sky.

L.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has multiplied you, and here you [are] today like the stars of the heavens for multitude.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has made your people grow. Now there are as many of you as there are stars in the sky.

decisions.choice: like the stars of the heavens: the promise to Abraham fulfilled
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham that his offspring would be as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5; 22:17; 26:4). Moses says the promise has come true (10:22). His trouble is not that the people are too many; that is God's blessing. The trouble is that one man cannot lead so many.

decisions.choice: like the stars for multitude: very many, a picture and not a count
decisions.reason: The comparison is a way of saying "beyond counting", as in 10:22 and 28:62. It does not give a number.

records.source: יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֽוֹתֵכֶ֗ם יֹסֵ֧ף עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם כָּכֶ֖ם אֶ֣לֶף פְּעָמִ֑ים וִיבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, may he add to you like you [are] a thousand times, and may he bless you just as he spoke to you.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, increase you a thousandfold beyond what you are now, and bless you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised!

L.11: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, add to you a thousand times as many as you [are], and bless you just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken to you!

R.11: I pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, will make you a thousand times more than you are now. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bless you, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised.

decisions.choice: may he add ... may he bless: a wish and a prayer
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form of a wish. Moses breaks off to bless the people's growth, so that no one hears his words in verse 9 as a complaint about their numbers.

decisions.choice: a thousand times: far more, without limit
decisions.reason: "A thousand times" is a way of saying "many times over". It is not a calculation.

decisions.choice: as he spoke to you: as he promised
decisions.reason: "Speak" here means to promise, as when God told Abraham he would bless him and make him a great nation (Genesis 12:2; 22:17).

decisions.choice: I pray that
decisions.reason: Readable turns the wish into a plain prayer, which is what "may he" expresses.

records.source: אֵיכָ֥ה אֶשָּׂ֖א לְבַדִּ֑י טָרְחֲכֶ֥ם וּמַֽשַּׂאֲכֶ֖ם וְרִֽיבְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: How will I bear by myself your trouble and your load and your strife?
pieces: How am I to carry on my own all your troubles, the load you put on me, and your quarrels?

L.12: How can I bear by myself your trouble and your load and your disputes?

R.12: How can I handle all your problems, your needs and your arguments by myself?

decisions.choice: trouble, load, strife: the weight of the people's needs and their quarrels
decisions.reason: Three words pile up the burden. The first means a heavy trouble (Isaiah 1:14 uses it for what God is weary of carrying); the second is a load to be carried; the third is a quarrel or lawsuit. The last points to the need for judges in verses 13-17.

decisions.choice: how can I bear: a question expecting the answer "I cannot"
decisions.reason: Moses does not ask for information; he is saying that the task is beyond one man (verse 9).

records.source: הָב֣וּ לָ֠כֶם אֲנָשִׁ֨ים חֲכָמִ֧ים וּנְבֹנִ֛ים וִידֻעִ֖ים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶ֑ם וַאֲשִׂימֵ֖ם בְּרָאשֵׁיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Provide for yourselves men wise and understanding and known, from your tribes, and I will set them as your heads.
pieces: From your tribes, pick men who are wise, discerning and well known, and I will put them at your head.'

L.13: Provide for yourselves men [who are] wise and understanding and known, from your tribes, and I will set them as your heads.'

R.13: Each tribe should choose men who are wise and have good sense, men whom people know and trust. Then I will make them your leaders.'

decisions.choice: wise, understanding and known: men of practical wisdom and good judgment, known and respected in their tribes
decisions.reason: "Wise" is skill in living and in handling matters; "understanding" is the ability to see what is right in a case (1 Kings 3:9, 12). "Known" means that their tribes know them and their character: they are proven men, not strangers. Exodus 18:21 adds that the leaders must fear God, be trustworthy and hate bribes.

decisions.choice: provide for yourselves ... and I will set them: the people choose and Moses appoints
decisions.reason: The people are to put forward the men, and Moses gives them their office. In Exodus 18:25 Moses himself chooses them; here he stresses the people's share in the choice, as their agreement in verse 14 does.

decisions.choice: men whom people know and trust
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what it means to be "known" in a tribe: to have a name people can rely on.

records.source: וַֽתַּעֲנ֖וּ אֹתִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ טֽוֹב־הַדָּבָ֥ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: And you answered me and said, Good [is] the thing which you have spoken to do.
pieces: You answered me, 'Your plan is a good one; let it be done.'

L.14: And you answered me and said, 'Good [is] the thing that you have spoken, to do [it].'

R.14: You answered, 'That is a good plan. Let us do it.'

decisions.choice: good to do: the people agree to the plan
decisions.reason: The people give their consent. Moses recalls it so that they remember the leaders were their own choice as well as his.

decisions.choice: plan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the word" or "the thing" that Moses had spoken. Balanced and Readable call it a plan, which is what it was.

records.source: וָאֶקַּ֞ח אֶת־רָאשֵׁ֣י שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֗ם אֲנָשִׁ֤ים חֲכָמִים֙ וִֽידֻעִ֔ים וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם רָאשִׁ֖ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם שָׂרֵ֨י אֲלָפִ֜ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֗וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֤י חֲמִשִּׁים֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י עֲשָׂרֹ֔ת וְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I took [the] heads of your tribes, men wise and known, and I set them [as] heads over you, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds and officers of fifties and officers of tens, and officials for your tribes.
pieces: So I took the leading men of your tribes, wise and respected men, and set them over you as leaders: commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of tens, and officials for each of your tribes.

L.15: So I took the heads of your tribes, men [who were] wise and known, and I made them heads over you, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds and officers of fifties and officers of tens, and officials for your tribes.

R.15: So I took the leaders of your tribes, men who were wise and well known, and put them in charge of you. Some led groups of a thousand people, some led a hundred, some fifty, and some ten. Others became officials for your tribes.

decisions.choice: officers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens: a ranked order of leaders
decisions.reason: The people are organized in groups of different sizes, each with its own leader, as in Exodus 18:21, 25. The same ranks are used for an army (Numbers 31:14, 48), and here they also serve to settle disputes (verses 16-17). How large a "thousand" was is discussed at Numbers 1.

decisions.choice: officials: men who kept records and carried out orders
decisions.reason: This word names officers who served under leaders and judges: the Israelite foremen in Egypt (Exodus 5:14-19), helpers of the elders (Numbers 11:16), and officers who gave orders to the army (20:5-9). Deuteronomy 16:18 sets them beside judges in every town.

decisions.choice: wise and known: the qualities asked for in verse 13
decisions.reason: Verse 15 names two of the three qualities in verse 13 and leaves out "understanding". The shorter list sums up the same request; it does not lower the standard.

decisions.choice: officers (Literal), commanders (Balanced), led (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for these leaders is used of princes, court officials and army captains. Here it names the leader of a group of a given size, so Literal says "officers", Balanced "commanders", and Readable says plainly what they did. Balanced keeps "officials" for the different word at the end of the verse.

records.source: וָאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת־שֹׁ֣פְטֵיכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁמֹ֤עַ בֵּין־אֲחֵיכֶם֙ וּשְׁפַטְתֶּ֣ם צֶ֔דֶק בֵּֽין־אִ֥ישׁ וּבֵין־אָחִ֖יו וּבֵ֥ין גֵּרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I commanded your judges at the time the that, saying, Hear between your brothers and judge righteously between a man and between his brother and between his sojourner.
pieces: At that time I gave your judges this charge: 'Hear the disputes among your {{gender:fellow Israelites|brothers}}, and judge fairly in every case, whether it is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a outsider living among you.

L.16: And I commanded your judges at that time, saying, 'Hear [cases] between your brothers, and judge rightly between a man and his brother and the sojourner [who is] with him.

R.16: At that time I told your judges, 'Listen carefully to the arguments between your {{gender:fellow Israelites|brothers}}. Judge fairly, whether the case is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a outsider who lives among you.

decisions.choice: hear between your brothers: hear both sides of a dispute
decisions.reason: To "hear between" two people is to listen to each party in a case before deciding it.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means a member of the same people, not a family member, as often in Deuteronomy (15:7; 17:15; 24:14). Disputes were brought by women as well as men (Numbers 27:1-5).

decisions.choice: righteously: by what is right, fairly and truly
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for what is right and just. A judgment is "righteous" when it gives each party what is right in God's eyes, without favor or bribe (16:18-20).

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a foreigner living in Israel
decisions.reason: The word names someone from outside who lives among a people without land or family there. Such people were easily wronged, and the law protects them again and again (10:18-19; 24:17; 27:19; Exodus 22:20). In court they are to get the same justice as an Israelite.

decisions.choice: between two Israelites or between an Israelite and an outsider
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "between a man and his brother and his sojourner". Balanced and Readable say what the two kinds of case are, which also lets them speak of any person rather than only of men.

records.source: לֹֽא־תַכִּ֨ירוּ פָנִ֜ים בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט כַּקָּטֹ֤ן כַּגָּדֹל֙ תִּשְׁמָע֔וּן לֹ֤א תָג֨וּרוּ֙ מִפְּנֵי־אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֥י הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט לֵאלֹהִ֣ים ה֑וּא וְהַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִקְשֶׁ֣ה מִכֶּ֔ם תַּקְרִב֥וּן אֵלַ֖י וּשְׁמַעְתִּֽיו׃
records.gloss: Not you will regard faces in the judgment; like the small like the great you will hear; not you will fear from [the] face of a man, for the judgment to God it [is]; and the matter which is too hard for you, you will bring near to me, and I will hear it.
pieces: In giving judgment, do not take anyone's side because of who they are. Give the humble and the powerful the same hearing. Fear no one, since the judgment is God's. If a case is too difficult for you, bring it to me and I will hear it.'

L.17: You shall not regard faces in judgment; you shall hear the small as well as the great. You shall not fear the face of anyone, for the judgment [belongs] to God. And the matter that is too hard for you, you shall bring near to me, and I will hear it.'

R.17: When you judge, do not favor anyone. Listen to unimportant people and important people in the same way. Do not be afraid of anyone, because you are judging for God. If a case is too hard for you, bring it to me, and I will decide it.'

decisions.choice: regard faces: show favor to a person because of who they are
decisions.reason: To "recognize the face" in court is to let a person's rank, wealth or friendship decide the case (16:19; Leviticus 19:15; Proverbs 24:23).

decisions.choice: the small and the great: everyone, the unimportant and the powerful alike
decisions.reason: The pair covers all people, poor and rich, weak and strong. Each must get the same hearing.

decisions.choice: fear the face of anyone: be intimidated by anyone
decisions.reason: A judge must not give way to threats or pressure from powerful people.

decisions.choice: the judgment belongs to God: judges act in God's place and answer to him
decisions.reason: Justice is God's own concern (10:17-18; 32:4). Those who judge do it on his behalf, so they have no need to fear people, and they will answer to him for their verdicts (2 Chronicles 19:6).

decisions.choice: because you are judging for God
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the judgment is God's" in terms of what it means for the judges (see the meaning decision). Readable also says "decide" for "hear" at the end, since hearing the case means judging it.

records.source: וָאֲצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑וא אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן׃
records.gloss: And I commanded you at the time the that all the things which you will do.
pieces: At that time I gave you instructions about everything you were to do.

L.18: And at that time I commanded you all the things that you are to do.

R.18: At that time I told you everything you were to do.

decisions.choice: I commanded you all the things you should do: the instructions given to the whole people at Horeb
decisions.reason: "You" is now the whole people, not only the judges. Moses sums up the commands given at Horeb before Israel set out, which he will set out again in chapters 5-26.

records.source: וַנִּסַּ֣ע מֵחֹרֵ֗ב וַנֵּ֡לֶךְ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַגָּדוֹל֩ וְהַנּוֹרָ֨א הַה֜וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְאִיתֶ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ הַ֣ר הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ אֹתָ֑נוּ וַנָּבֹ֕א עַ֖ד קָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: And we set out from Horeb and went through all the wilderness the great and the fearsome, that which you saw, [the] way of [the] hill country of the Amorite[s], just as had commanded Yahweh our God us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
pieces: We left Horeb and made our way through that whole vast and fearsome wilderness you have seen, along the road to the hill country of the Amorites, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.

L.19: And we set out from Horeb and went through all that great and fearsome wilderness that you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.

R.19: Then we left Horeb, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God had commanded us. We went through that huge and frightening desert that you saw, on the road toward the hill country of the Amorites. At last we came to Kadesh-barnea.

decisions.choice: fearsome: a wilderness that fills people with dread
decisions.reason: The word describes what causes fear. Deuteronomy 8:15 says what made this wilderness so: snakes and scorpions and thirsty ground without water.

decisions.choice: from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea: the journey told in Numbers 10-13
decisions.reason: Israel left the mountain in the second year (Numbers 10:11-12) and went through the wilderness of Paran to Kadesh, from where the spies were sent (Numbers 13:26). The route went north toward the hill country of Canaan, here called "the hill country of the Amorites" (see verse 7).

decisions.choice: that you saw: the hearers themselves witnessed it
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Moses speaks to the people in Moab as those who made the journey, so that the past becomes their own experience.

decisions.choice: Then we left Horeb, as the LORD our God had commanded us.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the command next to the setting out, which it governs, and breaks the long sentence into three.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵכֶ֑ם בָּאתֶם֙ עַד־הַ֣ר הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And I said to you, You have come to [the] hill country of the Amorite[s] which Yahweh our God [is] giving to us.
pieces: I told you, 'Now you are at the hill country of the Amorites, the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving us.

L.20: And I said to you, 'You have come as far as the hill country of the Amorites, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God [is] giving to us.

R.20: I said to you, 'Now you have come to the hill country of the Amorites. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving it to us.

decisions.choice: is giving: the gift is already under way
decisions.reason: The verb form describes something happening now or about to happen. The land is not a distant hope; God is in the act of giving it (verse 25).

records.source: רְ֠אֵה נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ לְפָנֶ֖יךָ אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ עֲלֵ֣ה רֵ֗שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ לָ֔ךְ אַל־תִּירָ֖א וְאַל־תֵּחָֽת׃
records.gloss: See, has set Yahweh your God before you the land; go up, take possession, just as has spoken Yahweh [the] God of your fathers to you; not do fear and not be dismayed.
pieces: Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession of it, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, told you. Do not be afraid or lose heart.'

L.21: See, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has set before you the land. Go up, take possession, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, spoke to you. Do not fear, and do not be dismayed.'

R.21: Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land. Go up and take it, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, told you to do. Do not be afraid, and do not lose courage.'

decisions.choice: you (singular): Moses addresses the people as one
decisions.reason: In verse 20 "you" is plural; in verse 21 it is singular. Deuteronomy often moves between the two, sometimes speaking to the people as a crowd and sometimes as one body. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: go up, take possession: Moses repeats God's command of verse 8
decisions.reason: The words echo God's command at Horeb (verse 8): the land is set before them, and they have only to go up and take it.

decisions.choice: do not fear and do not be dismayed: do not lose courage
decisions.reason: The second verb means to be shattered or broken down with fear. The same pair encourages Joshua (31:8; Joshua 1:9; 8:1).

records.source: וַתִּקְרְב֣וּן אֵלַי֮ כֻּלְּכֶם֒ וַתֹּאמְר֗וּ נִשְׁלְחָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ וְיַחְפְּרוּ־לָ֖נוּ אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיָשִׁ֤בוּ אֹתָ֨נוּ֙ דָּבָ֔ר אֶת־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲלֶה־בָּ֔הּ וְאֵת֙ הֶֽעָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָבֹ֖א אֲלֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And you came near to me, all of you, and said, Let us send men before us, and let them search out for us the land and bring back to us word [of] the way which we will go up by it and the cities which we will come to them.
pieces: Then you all came to me and said, 'Let us send men on ahead to explore the land for us. They can come back and tell us which way to go up and what towns we will meet.'

L.22: And you came near to me, all of you, and said, 'Let us send men ahead of us, so that they may search out the land for us and bring back word to us [about] the way by which we should go up and the cities to which we will come.'

R.22: Then all of you came to me. You said, 'Let us send some men ahead of us to look over the land. They can come back and tell us which road to take and which towns we will come to.'

decisions.choice: let us send men: the request that led to the sending of the spies (Numbers 13)
decisions.reason: Numbers 13:1-2 tells the sending of the twelve as the LORD's command to Moses. Here Moses recalls that the request came first from the people and that he agreed (verse 23). The two accounts look at the same event from different sides.

decisions.choice: search out: explore and gather information
decisions.reason: The verb means to dig or search, and so to find out about a place. The men are to report on the routes and the towns, as a scouting party would.

records.source: וַיִּיטַ֥ב בְּעֵינַ֖י הַדָּבָ֑ר וָאֶקַּ֤ח מִכֶּם֙ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲנָשִׁ֔ים אִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד לַשָּֽׁבֶט׃
records.gloss: And was good in my eyes the thing, and I took from you twelve men, one man for a tribe.
pieces: I agreed with the plan, and I chose twelve of your men, one from each tribe.

L.23: And the thing was good in my eyes, and I took from you twelve men, one man for a tribe.

R.23: I thought it was a good plan. So I chose twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.

decisions.choice: good in my eyes: it seemed right to me
decisions.reason: "In my eyes" means in my judgment.

decisions.choice: twelve men, one for each tribe: the spies named in Numbers 13:4-16
decisions.reason: Each tribe had a share in the mission, so that the report would come from the whole people. Numbers 13:4-16 lists their names, among them Caleb and Joshua (verses 36, 38).

records.source: וַיִּפְנוּ֙ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ הָהָ֔רָה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־נַ֣חַל אֶשְׁכֹּ֑ל וַֽיְרַגְּל֖וּ אֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And they turned and went up to the hill country and came to [the] valley of Eshcol and spied it out.
pieces: They set out and went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.

L.24: And they turned and went up to the hill country, and came as far as the Valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.

R.24: They went up into the hill country and came to the Eshcol Valley, and they explored the land.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Eshcol: a valley near Hebron, named for a cluster of grapes
decisions.reason: Eshcol means "cluster". Numbers 13:22-24 tells how the spies cut a cluster of grapes there so large that two men carried it on a pole.

decisions.choice: spied it out: the land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word "it" is feminine, matching "land" rather than "valley". The spies explored the land, as Numbers 13:21 says they went through it from south to north.

decisions.choice: the land
decisions.reason: Readable names what "it" refers to (see the meaning decision).

records.source: וַיִּקְח֤וּ בְיָדָם֙ מִפְּרִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיּוֹרִ֖דוּ אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וַיָּשִׁ֨בוּ אֹתָ֤נוּ דָבָר֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ טוֹבָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And they took in their hand from [the] fruit of the land and brought [it] down to us, and brought back to us word and said, Good [is] the land which Yahweh our God [is] giving to us.
pieces: They took some of the land's fruit with them and brought it down to us. And they gave us their report: 'The land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving us is good.'

L.25: And they took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought [it] down to us, and they brought back word to us and said, 'Good [is] the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving to us.'

R.25: They brought some of the fruit of the land back down to us. They told us, 'The land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving us is a good land.'

decisions.choice: good is the land: the report Moses recalls is the good one
decisions.reason: Numbers 13:27-33 tells that the spies praised the land but most of them also spread fear about its people. Moses recalls here the part that left Israel without excuse: the land was good, and God was giving it, as Joshua and Caleb said (Numbers 14:7-8). The fear comes out in verse 28.

decisions.choice: brought down: from the hill country to the camp at Kadesh
decisions.reason: Kadesh lay in the lower land to the south, so the spies came down from the hills with the fruit.

records.source: וְלֹ֥א אֲבִיתֶ֖ם לַעֲלֹ֑ת וַתַּמְר֕וּ אֶת־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: But not you were willing to go up, and you rebelled against [the] mouth of Yahweh your God.
pieces: But you refused to go up, and set yourselves against the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.26: But you were not willing to go up, and you rebelled against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.26: But you would not go up. You turned against what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God had commanded.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the LORD: his spoken command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what is spoken. To rebel against God's mouth is to defy what he has said (verse 43; 9:23).

decisions.choice: rebelled: openly defied
decisions.reason: The verb means stubborn defiance against one's rightful authority. Moses uses it of the whole wilderness generation (9:7, 23-24; 31:27).

decisions.choice: the mouth of
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced says "command" and Readable "what ... had commanded". Balanced says "set yourselves against" for the verb "rebel" (see the meaning decision).

records.source: וַתֵּרָגְנ֤וּ בְאָהֳלֵיכֶם֙ וַתֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ בְּשִׂנְאַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔נוּ הוֹצִיאָ֖נוּ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לָתֵ֥ת אֹתָ֛נוּ בְּיַ֥ד הָאֱמֹרִ֖י לְהַשְׁמִידֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And you grumbled in your tents and said, In [the] hatred of Yahweh [for] us he has brought us out from [the] land of Egypt to give us into [the] hand of the Amorite[s] to destroy us.
pieces: You complained in your tents and said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates us. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought us out of Egypt: to hand us over to the Amorites to wipe us out.

L.27: And you grumbled in your tents and said, 'Out of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hatred for us {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought us out from the land of Egypt to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

R.27: You complained in your tents. You said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates us! That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought us out of Egypt. He wants to hand us over to the Amorites so that they can kill us.

decisions.choice: because the LORD hates us: the people turn the rescue from Egypt into a sign of hate
decisions.reason: The rescue from Egypt was the great proof of God's love (4:37; 7:8). In their fear the people say the opposite, that God freed them only to destroy them. Moses quotes their words so that the hearers see how deep the unbelief went.

decisions.choice: grumbled in your tents: complaining among themselves, in private
decisions.reason: The grumbling was not a public protest but talk spread from tent to tent (Psalm 106:25).

decisions.choice: give us into the hand of: hand us over to the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control.

records.source: אָנָ֣ה׀אֲנַ֣חְנוּ עֹלִ֗ים אַחֵינוּ֩ הֵמַ֨סּוּ אֶת־לְבָבֵ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר עַ֣ם גָּד֤וֹל וָרָם֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ עָרִ֛ים גְּדֹלֹ֥ת וּבְצוּרֹ֖ת בַּשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְגַם־בְּנֵ֥י עֲנָקִ֖ים רָאִ֥ינוּ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: Where [are] we going up? Our brothers have made melt our heart, saying, A people greater and taller than we, cities great and fortified in the heavens; and also sons of [the] Anakim we saw there.
pieces: Where are we going up to? Our brothers have made us lose heart. They say, "The people are bigger and taller than we are, the cities are large, with walls up to the sky, and we even saw the descendants of the Anakim there."'

L.28: To where [are] we going up? Our brothers have melted our heart, saying, "A people greater and taller than we; cities great and walled up to the heavens; and also the sons of the Anakim we saw there."'

R.28: How can we go up there? Our own men have made us afraid. They told us, "The people there are bigger and taller than we are. Their cities are large, and their walls reach up to the sky. We even saw the descendants of Anak there!"'

decisions.choice: where are we going up: a cry of despair, not a question about the route
decisions.reason: The people do not ask for directions; they mean that there is nowhere they can safely go.

decisions.choice: made our hearts melt: took away our courage
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and courage. A melting heart is one that gives way to fear (20:8; Joshua 2:11; 5:1). "Our brothers" are the spies who brought the frightening report.

decisions.choice: fortified up to the heavens: walls that look sky-high
decisions.reason: The phrase is an exaggeration born of fear, as in 9:1. It describes how the walls looked to the spies.

decisions.choice: the sons of the Anakim: a people known for their great size
decisions.reason: The Anakim lived around Hebron (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33; Joshua 14:12-15). Their height became a byword (2:10-11, 21; 9:2).

decisions.choice: How can we go up there? Our own men
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cry of despair as a plain question of "how", and calls the spies "our own men", since "brothers" here means fellow Israelites.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵכֶ֑ם לֹא־תַֽעַרְצ֥וּן וְֽלֹא־תִֽירְא֖וּן מֵהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I said to you, Not you will be terrified and not you will fear from them.
pieces: Then I said to you, 'Do not tremble; do not be afraid of them.

L.29: And I said to you, 'Do not be terrified, and do not be afraid of them.

R.29: I told you, 'Do not be terrified. Do not be afraid of them.

decisions.choice: be terrified ... be afraid: do not give way to dread
decisions.reason: The first verb means to tremble with dread before something overwhelming; the second is the ordinary word for fear. Moses uses them again when he sends Israel to war (7:21; 20:3; 31:6).

records.source: יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ הַהֹלֵ֣ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם ה֖וּא יִלָּחֵ֣ם לָכֶ֑ם כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה אִתְּכֶ֛ם בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Yahweh your God, the one going before you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did with you in Egypt before your eyes,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who goes ahead of you, is the one who will fight for you, as you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do for you in Egypt,

L.30: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God, the one going before you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will fight for you, according to all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did for you in Egypt before your eyes,

R.30: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going ahead of you. He will fight for you, just as you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do for you in Egypt.

decisions.choice: the LORD goes before you and fights for you: God as the one who leads Israel's army
decisions.reason: God had fought for Israel at the sea (Exodus 14:14, 25), and Moses promises that he will do so again (3:22; 20:4; 31:8). Israel's fear left him out of the account.

decisions.choice: he will fight: he himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "he" for emphasis: it is the LORD, not Israel's own strength, who will fight.

decisions.choice: before your eyes: you saw it yourselves
decisions.reason: The people had seen the plagues and the crossing of the sea with their own eyes (4:34; 29:1).

decisions.choice: is the one who will fight
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the emphatic pronoun with "is the one who"; Literal keeps "he". Balanced and Readable also say "you saw him do" for "before your eyes".

records.source: וּבַמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֔יתָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נְשָׂאֲךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׂא־אִ֖ישׁאֶת־בְּנ֑וֹ בְּכָל־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲלַכְתֶּ֔ם עַד־בֹּאֲכֶ֖ם עַד־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: and in the wilderness, where you saw that carried you Yahweh your God as carries a man his son, in all the way which you walked until your coming to the place the this.
pieces: and in the wilderness. There you saw how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God carried you the whole way you traveled, as a father carries his son, until you arrived here.'

L.31: and in the wilderness, where you saw that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God carried you as a man carries his son, in all the way that you walked, until you came to this place.'

R.31: You also saw it in the desert: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God carried you all along the way until you came to this place, just as a father carries his child.'

decisions.choice: as a man carries his son: God's care for Israel pictured as a father carrying his child
decisions.reason: The picture is of a father lifting a tired child and carrying him on a long journey. It shows the tenderness of God's care in the wilderness, as also in 32:10-11, Hosea 11:3 and Isaiah 46:3-4. It answers the people's charge that God hated them (verse 27).

decisions.choice: this place: Kadesh, where Moses first spoke these words
decisions.reason: Moses is quoting what he said to the people at Kadesh (verse 29), so "this place" is Kadesh at the edge of the land.

decisions.choice: a father carries his son / his child
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a man carries his son"; the man carrying his own son is a father, so Balanced and Readable say so. Readable says "child", since the picture is of any young child.

records.source: וּבַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה אֵֽינְכֶם֙ מַאֲמִינִ֔ם בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And in the thing the this you [were] not trusting in Yahweh your God,
pieces: Yet for all this you did not trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,

L.32: Yet in this matter you were not trusting in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,

R.32: But even so, you did not trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: in this thing: in spite of this
decisions.reason: The words can mean "in spite of this word", that is, in spite of Moses' assurance in verses 29-31 and all that God had done, or "in this matter", the matter of going up into the land. Either way, the people's unbelief is set against God's proven care.

decisions.choice: trusting: relying on God and his word
decisions.reason: The verb means to rely on someone as firm and trustworthy. It is the word used of Abraham, who trusted God (Genesis 15:6); here it is denied of Israel, as in Numbers 14:11 and Deuteronomy 9:23.

decisions.choice: you did not trust: Moses speaks directly to his hearers again
decisions.reason: Moses' quotation of his words at Kadesh ends with verse 31, and verses 32-33 are his comment to the people in Moab. The Hebrew has no quotation marks, and the words could also be read as the end of what he said at Kadesh; the meaning is the same.

records.source: הַהֹלֵ֨ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶ֜ם בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ לָת֥וּר לָכֶ֛ם מָק֖וֹם לַֽחֲנֹֽתְכֶ֑ם בָּאֵ֣שׁ׀לַ֗יְלָה לַרְאֹֽתְכֶם֙ בַּדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽלְכוּ־בָ֔הּ וּבֶעָנָ֖ן יוֹמָֽם׃
records.gloss: the one going before you on the way to seek out for you a place for your camping, in fire by night to show you the way which you should go in it, and in [the] cloud by day.
pieces: who went ahead of you on the way to look for places for you to camp, in fire by night to show you which way to go, and in the cloud by day.

L.33: the one going before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way that you should go, and in the cloud by day.

R.33: He went ahead of you on your journey to find places for you to camp. At night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in a fire to show you the way to go, and by day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in a cloud.

decisions.choice: in fire by night and in the cloud by day: the pillar of cloud and fire
decisions.reason: God led Israel by a pillar of cloud by day and of fire by night (Exodus 13:21-22; Numbers 9:15-23). Numbers 10:33-34 says that the ark went ahead of the people to seek out a place for them to rest, and the cloud was over them.

decisions.choice: to seek out: God himself scouted the way
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for spying out the land in Numbers 13. Israel sent men to scout the land, though God had always gone ahead to find their way and their camping places.

decisions.choice: He went ahead of you
decisions.reason: Readable makes a new sentence of the description, with "He" for the LORD, and breaks the rest into two clauses.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ק֣וֹל דִּבְרֵיכֶ֑ם וַיִּקְצֹ֖ף וַיִּשָּׁבַ֥ע לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And heard Yahweh [the] sound of your words, and he was angry and swore, saying,
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard what you said, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry and swore an oath:

L.34: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard the sound of your words, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry and swore, saying,

R.34: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard what you were saying, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became angry. He swore,

decisions.choice: the sound of your words: the grumbling in the tents
decisions.reason: God heard the complaining of verses 27-28, though it was spoken in the tents.

decisions.choice: he was angry and swore: God's oath at Kadesh, told in Numbers 14:20-35
decisions.reason: Numbers 14:21-23 and 28-30 give the oath in fuller form: the men who refused would die in the wilderness, and only Caleb and Joshua would enter.

records.source: אִם־יִרְאֶ֥ה אִישׁ֙ בָּאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה הַדּ֥וֹר הָרָ֖ע הַזֶּ֑ה אֵ֚ת הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֔עְתִּי לָתֵ֖ת לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: If will see a man among the men the these, the generation the evil the this, the land the good which I swore to give to your fathers,
pieces: 'Of these men, this evil generation, not a single one will see the good land that I swore I would give your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}},

L.35: 'Not one man among these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,

R.35: 'Not one of these men from this evil generation will see the good land that I promised with an oath to give to your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

decisions.choice: if one sees: the form of an oath, meaning "not one will see"
decisions.reason: Hebrew oaths often begin "if ..." and leave the curse unspoken: "if this happens, may I ...". The sense is a strong denial, "not one shall see" (Numbers 14:23, 30; Psalm 95:11).

decisions.choice: this evil generation: the grown men who refused to enter
decisions.reason: These are the men counted from twenty years old and up (Numbers 14:29), who as a body refused the land. Deuteronomy 2:14-16 tells that they all died in the wilderness before Israel crossed the Zered.

decisions.choice: Not one man ... shall see
decisions.reason: Literal does not keep the oath's "if", which English cannot read as a denial; it gives the meaning of the formula (see the meaning decision).

records.source: זֽוּלָתִ֞י כָּלֵ֤ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּה֙ ה֣וּא יִרְאֶ֔נָּה וְלֽוֹ־אֶתֵּ֧ן אֶת־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דָּֽרַךְ־בָּ֖הּ וּלְבָנָ֑יו יַ֕עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִלֵּ֖א אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: except Caleb son of Jephunneh; he will see it, and to him I will give the land which he has trodden on, and to his sons, because that he has filled after Yahweh.
pieces: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his descendants the land he walked on, because he followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wholeheartedly.'

L.36: except Caleb son of Jephunneh; he will see it, and to him I will give the land that he set foot on, and to his {{gender:children|sons}}, because he followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fully.'

R.36: Only Caleb son of Jephunneh will see it. He followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all his heart. So I will give him and his descendants the land he walked on.'

decisions.choice: he filled after the LORD: he followed the LORD fully
decisions.reason: To "fill after" someone is to follow them completely, holding nothing back, as in Numbers 14:24 and 32:12 and Joshua 14:8-9, 14.

decisions.choice: the land on which he has trodden: Hebron, where Caleb went as a spy
decisions.reason: Caleb went through the land as far as Hebron (Numbers 13:22), and Joshua 14:6-14 tells how he received it for his family. Treading on land is a sign of claiming it (11:24; Joshua 1:3). His family's share included his daughter's (Joshua 15:16-19).

decisions.choice: followed the LORD: God names himself
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, God speaks of himself by name in the third person within his own words.

records.source: גַּם־בִּי֙ הִתְאַנַּ֣ף יְהוָ֔ה בִּגְלַלְכֶ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר גַּם־אַתָּ֖ה לֹא־תָבֹ֥א שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: Also with me was angry Yahweh on account of you, saying, Also you, not you will enter there.
pieces: Because of you {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me too, and said, 'You will not go in there either.

L.37: Also with me {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry because of you, saying, 'You too shall not enter there.

R.37: Because of you, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me too. He said, 'You will not go into the land either.

decisions.choice: on your account: Moses links his own exclusion with the people's rebellion
decisions.reason: Numbers 20:12 and 27:14 tell that Moses and Aaron were kept out of the land because they did not honor God at the waters of Meribah. Moses says here, and again in 3:26 and 4:21, that it happened because of the people: their quarrel led to his failure, and he shares the fate of their generation. Both accounts stand side by side in Deuteronomy (32:51).

decisions.choice: also with me: an event later than Kadesh, told here with it
decisions.reason: God's anger with Moses came near the end of the wilderness years (Numbers 20). Moses mentions it here because it belongs with the oath at Kadesh: it settles who will and who will not enter the land.

decisions.choice: into the land
decisions.reason: Readable says where "there" is.

records.source: יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בִּןנוּן֙ הָעֹמֵ֣ד לְפָנֶ֔יךָ ה֖וּא יָ֣בֹא שָׁ֑מָּה אֹת֣וֹ חַזֵּ֔ק כִּי־ה֖וּא יַנְחִלֶ֥נָּה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Joshua son of Nun, the one standing before you, he will enter there; him strengthen, for he will cause to inherit it Israel.
pieces: Joshua son of Nun, your assistant, is the one who will go in. Encourage him, because he will lead Israel to take the land as their inheritance.

L.38: Joshua son of Nun, who is standing before you, he is the one who will enter there. Make him strong, for he will cause Israel to inherit it.

R.38: Joshua son of Nun, your helper, will go in. Give him courage, because he is the one who will lead Israel to take the land for their own.

decisions.choice: standing before you: serving you as your attendant
decisions.reason: To "stand before" someone is to wait on them and serve them. Joshua was Moses' assistant from his youth (Exodus 24:13; 33:11; Numbers 11:28).

decisions.choice: strengthen him, make him strong: give him courage and firmness
decisions.reason: The verb means to make strong. Moses is to put heart into Joshua for the task ahead, as he does in 3:28 and 31:7, 23.

decisions.choice: cause Israel to inherit it: lead Israel to receive the land as its family inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb means to give an inheritance. Joshua will lead the conquest and divide the land among the tribes as their lasting family property (Joshua 11:23; 14:1).

records.source: וְטַפְּכֶם֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֜ם לָבַ֣ז יִהְיֶ֗ה וּ֠בְנֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־יָדְע֤וּ הַיּוֹם֙ ט֣וֹב וָרָ֔ע הֵ֖מָּה יָבֹ֣אוּ שָׁ֑מָּה וְלָהֶ֣ם אֶתְּנֶ֔נָּה וְהֵ֖ם יִירָשֽׁוּהָּ׃
records.gloss: And your little ones, who you said for plunder will become, and your sons who not know today good and evil, they will enter there, and to them I will give it, and they will take possession of it.
pieces: And your little ones, whom you said would be carried off as plunder, and your {{gender:children|sons}}, who today cannot yet tell good from evil, they are the ones who will go in. I will give the land to them, and they will take possession of it.

L.39: And your little ones, who you said would become plunder, and your {{gender:children|sons}}, who today do not know good and evil, they will enter there; and to them I will give it, and they will take possession of it.

R.39: But your little ones will go in, the young children who are still too young to know right from wrong. You said enemies would capture them. But I will give the land to them, and they will take it as their own.

decisions.choice: your little ones, who you said would become plunder: the people's fear turned around
decisions.reason: At Kadesh the people complained that their wives and little ones would be taken as plunder (Numbers 14:3). God answers that those very children will enter the land (Numbers 14:31).

decisions.choice: who do not know good and evil: too young to be held responsible
decisions.reason: The phrase describes children not yet old enough to make moral choices (Isaiah 7:15-16). These are the ones under twenty, who were not counted with the generation that refused (Numbers 14:29).

decisions.choice: the clause about the little ones and plunder is read as part of the text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text includes "and your little ones, who you said would become plunder". The ancient Greek translation is reported to lack these words, and some think they were added to match Numbers 14:31. The translation follows the Hebrew text. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: your little ones ... the young children
decisions.reason: Readable takes "little ones" and "sons" together as the children of the people, and puts the complaint about them in a sentence of its own.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֖ם פְּנ֣וּ לָכֶ֑ם וּסְע֥וּ הַמִּדְבָּ֖רָה דֶּ֥רֶךְ יַם־סֽוּף׃
records.gloss: But you, turn for yourselves and set out to the wilderness, [the] way of [the] Sea of Reed[s].
pieces: But as for you, turn around and set out into the wilderness along the road to the Red Sea.'

L.40: But you, turn and set out into the wilderness [by] the way of the Sea of Reeds.'

R.40: But as for you, turn around and go back into the desert, toward the Red Sea.'

decisions.choice: the way of the Sea of Reeds: the road toward the gulf to the southeast
decisions.reason: The name is the one used for the sea of the crossing (Exodus 13:18; 15:4), known as the Red Sea. Here, as in Numbers 14:25, it most likely means the road toward the gulf east of Sinai, near Elath and Ezion-geber (2:1, 8). Israel is sent back the way it came, away from the land.

decisions.choice: turn and set out: the command of verse 7 reversed
decisions.reason: At Horeb God said "turn and set out" toward the land (verse 7). Now the same words send the people back into the wilderness.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in Exodus and Numbers, Literal says "Sea of Reeds", the meaning of the name, and Balanced and Readable "the Red Sea", the name English readers know.

records.source: וַֽתַּעֲנ֣וּ׀וַתֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלַ֗י חָטָאנוּ֮ לַֽיהוָה֒ אֲנַ֤חְנוּ נַעֲלֶה֙ וְנִלְחַ֔מְנוּ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖נוּ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽתַּחְגְּר֗וּ אִ֚ישׁ אֶת־כְּלֵ֣י מִלְחַמְתּ֔וֹ וַתָּהִ֖ינוּ לַעֲלֹ֥ת הָהָֽרָה׃
records.gloss: And you answered and said to me, We have sinned against Yahweh; we will go up and fight according to all that commanded us Yahweh our God. And you girded on, each man, his weapons of war and thought it easy to go up to the hill country.
pieces: Then you replied to me, 'We have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. We will go up and fight, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God commanded us.' So each of you strapped on his weapons, thinking it would be easy to go up into the hill country.

L.41: And you answered and said to me, 'We have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. We will go up and fight, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God commanded us.' And each man of you girded on his weapons of war, and you treated [it] as easy to go up into the hill country.

R.41: Then you answered me, 'We have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Now we will go and fight, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God told us to.' So every man put on his weapons. You thought it would be easy to go up into the hill country.

decisions.choice: we have sinned ... we will go up: a confession followed by a new disobedience
decisions.reason: The people admit their sin but try to undo it on their own terms. The command to go up (verses 8, 21) had been replaced by the command to turn back (verse 40), so going up now is a second rebellion (verse 43; Numbers 14:39-45).

decisions.choice: thought it easy: treated the attack lightly
decisions.reason: This verb occurs only here, and its sense is not certain. It is usually taken to mean "consider easy" or "make light of"; others take it as "dare" or "be eager". Each fits the picture of men rushing into battle without God.

decisions.choice: girded on his weapons of war: armed himself for battle
decisions.reason: Weapons such as a sword were fastened at the waist with a belt; "to gird" is to arm oneself (1 Samuel 25:13).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֱמֹ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לֹ֤א תַֽעֲלוּ֙ וְלֹא־תִלָּ֣חֲמ֔וּ כִּ֥י אֵינֶ֖נִּי בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וְלֹא֙ תִּנָּֽגְפ֔וּ לִפְנֵ֖י אֹיְבֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, Say to them, Not you shall go up and not you shall fight, for not I [am] in your midst, and not you will be struck down before your enemies.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Tell them, "Do not go up, and do not fight. I am not among you, and if you go, your enemies will strike you down."'

L.42: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Say to them, "Do not go up and do not fight, for I [am] not in your midst, so that you are not struck down before your enemies."'

R.42: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Tell them, "Do not go up and do not fight. I am not with you. If you go, your enemies will beat you."'

decisions.choice: I am not in your midst: without God's presence there is no victory
decisions.reason: In verse 30 the LORD was to go ahead of Israel and fight for them. Now he will not go with them (Numbers 14:42-43), so the attack can only fail (verse 44).

decisions.choice: and not be struck down: so that you are not defeated
decisions.reason: The last clause gives the purpose of the warning: do not go, so that you will not be struck down. It also implies what will happen if they go.

decisions.choice: if you go
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain what the warning implies (see the meaning decision).

records.source: וָאֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וַתַּמְרוּ֙ אֶת־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתָּזִ֖דוּ וַתַּעֲל֥וּ הָהָֽרָה׃
records.gloss: And I spoke to you, and not you listened, and you rebelled against [the] mouth of Yahweh, and acted presumptuously and went up to the hill country.
pieces: I warned you, but you paid no attention. You set yourselves against the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in your pride went up into the hill country.

L.43: And I spoke to you, and you did not listen; and you rebelled against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and you acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.

R.43: I told you this, but you would not listen. You turned against what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded. You were too proud to obey, and you went up into the hill country.

decisions.choice: acted presumptuously: acted in proud self-will
decisions.reason: The verb describes boiling over with pride, doing what one has decided against the word of God or of those he has set in charge (17:12-13; 18:22).

decisions.choice: you rebelled against the mouth of the LORD: the same rebellion as in verse 26, the other way round
decisions.reason: First the people refused to go up when God said go (verse 26); now they go up when God says do not go. In both cases they set their own will against his word.

decisions.choice: listen: obey
decisions.reason: To listen in Hebrew often means to heed and obey.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֨א הָאֱמֹרִ֜י הַיֹּשֵׁ֨ב בָּהָ֤ר הַהוּא֙ לִקְרַאתְכֶ֔ם וַיִּרְדְּפ֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ינָה הַדְּבֹרִ֑ים וַֽיַּכְּת֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֛ם בְּשֵׂעִ֖יר עַד־חָרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And came out the Amorite[s], the one dwelling in the hill country the that, to meet you, and they chased you as do the bees, and they beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
pieces: The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees. They cut you down in Seir, all the way to Hormah.

L.44: And the Amorites who dwelt in that hill country came out to meet you and pursued you as the bees do, and crushed you in Seir as far as Hormah.

R.44: The Amorites who lived in those hills came out to fight you. They chased you like a swarm of bees. They beat you badly in Seir and chased you all the way to Hormah.

decisions.choice: as bees do: in great numbers and without letting up
decisions.reason: A swarm of bees attacks in a mass and keeps after anyone who disturbs it (Psalm 118:12; Isaiah 7:18).

decisions.choice: the Amorites, Seir, Hormah: the defeat told in Numbers 14:45
decisions.reason: Numbers 14:45 names the Amalekites and the Canaanites; here "Amorites" stands for the peoples of the hill country as a whole (see verse 7). Seir is here the region south of the Negev, and Hormah a town in the Negev (Numbers 21:3).

decisions.choice: beat you down: crushed you
decisions.reason: The verb means to beat or crush to pieces. The defeat was severe.

decisions.choice: to meet you: to meet you in battle
decisions.reason: "To meet" here means to come out against an enemy.

records.source: וַתָּשֻׁ֥בוּ וַתִּבְכּ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־שָׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ בְּקֹ֣לְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א הֶאֱזִ֖ין אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you returned and wept before Yahweh, and not listened Yahweh to your voice and not gave ear to you.
pieces: Then you came back and wept before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would not listen to your cry or pay any attention to you.

L.45: And you came back and wept before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not listen to your voice, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not give ear to you.

R.45: Then you came back and cried in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would not listen to you or pay attention to what you said.

decisions.choice: wept before the LORD: mourning in God's presence, at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: To weep "before the LORD" is to lament and plead at the place of his presence (Judges 20:23, 26). The people mourned too late, after the defeat (Numbers 14:39).

decisions.choice: the LORD did not listen: an answer to the people's own refusal
decisions.reason: Israel did not listen to the LORD (verse 43), and now the LORD does not listen to Israel. The same verb is used both times.

decisions.choice: give ear: pay attention
decisions.reason: To "give ear" is to turn one's ear toward someone, to attend to them.

records.source: וַתֵּשְׁב֥וּ בְקָדֵ֖שׁ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים כַּיָּמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְשַׁבְתֶּֽם׃
records.gloss: And you stayed in Kadesh many days, like the days which you stayed.
pieces: So you stayed at Kadesh for a long time, all the time that you stayed there.

L.46: And you stayed in Kadesh many days, like the days that you stayed.

R.46: So you stayed in Kadesh a long time, as long as you did.

decisions.choice: many days, like the days that you stayed: a long time, however long it was
decisions.reason: The repetition leaves the length open: "you stayed as long as you stayed". The point is that the stay was long. The years in the wilderness from Kadesh until the crossing of the Zered were thirty-eight in all (2:14), and Kadesh was Israel's main camp in that time (Numbers 20:1).
